Free, Sovereign and Independent Republic of Sri Lanka

land.text: the whole island: 'As a British crown colony, the island was known as Ceylon; it achieved independence as the Dominion of Ceylon in 1948.'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria carries Ceylon inside its British Raj shape from 1859 to 1947; its own British Ceylon row stops in 1814.

capitals.name: Colombo
capitals.note: The Kotte page: 'Sri Lanka formally changed its administrative capital from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte in 1982.' Colombo stays the executive and judicial seat (Sri Lanka page infobox).

capitals.name: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte
capitals.note: Designated the new capital in 1977; the Parliament opened there on 29 April 1982. Infobox: 'Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (legislative); Colombo (executive and judicial)'. Coordinates 6 55 N 79 55 E from the page.

keyframe_review.note: 73,532 km2 for 1948-2023 against the infobox's 67,240 km2 (ratio 1.09; the page's provincial table totals 65,610 km2): the island with its coast cells, inside the factor of two. It is the whole island, including the Northern and Eastern provinces that the LTTE held in 1990-2009 (see the tamil-eelam rebel dossier and the ledger's loss and gain events).
Same outline as 1948-2023. Kachchatheevu (ceded by India in 1974) is smaller than a grid cell.

ledger.note: 4 February 1948: Ceylon becomes independent. 'The Soulbury constitution ushered in dominion status, with independence proclaimed on 4 February 1948'; 'it achieved independence as the Dominion of Ceylon in 1948', D. S. Senanayake its first prime minister.
22 May 1972: the Dominion becomes a republic. Infobox 'Republic: 22 May 1972'; 'In 1972, its formal name was changed to Free, Sovereign and Independent Republic of Sri Lanka'.

region.text: Kachchatheevu, a small island in Palk Strait

ledger.note: 1974: Kachchatheevu is ceded to Sri Lanka. 'In 1974, Kachchatheevu, a small island in Palk Strait, was formally ceded to Sri Lanka', tied on the page to the Sirima-Gandhi Pact of 1974. The page does not name India as the ceding party in one sentence, and the island is smaller than a grid cell.
7 September 1978: the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka. 'Later, on 7 September 1978, it was changed to the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka'.

1982: the capital moves from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte. 'Sri Lanka formally changed its administrative capital from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte in 1982'; designated in 1977, the move marked by the opening of Parliament on 29 April 1982. Colombo remains the executive and judicial seat.

region.text: Jaffna peninsula and the Kilinochchi district, the LTTE's northern core

ledger.note: 1989-90: the Tamil Tigers take the north. 'When the Indian Peace-Keeping Force withdrew in 1989-90, the LTTE established many government-like functions in the areas under its control' and 'swiftly took control of a significant portion of the territory'; the IPKF's last ship left on 24 March 1990, and in 1990 the army 'tried to retake Jaffna but failed'. The page names no district for 1990; Jaffna and Kilinochchi (the Jaffna stronghold and the Vanni seat) are the researcher's reading.

5 December 1995: the army retakes Jaffna. Operation Riviresa brought 'Jaffna under government control for the first time in nearly a decade'; the national flag was raised 'inside the Jaffna Fort on 5 December 1995'. Over 350,000 civilians fled to the Vanni.

region.text: the Mullaitivu district around the town where the army base fell

ledger.note: 18 July 1996: the Tigers overrun Mullaitivu. The LTTE 'decisively won the Battle of Mullaitivu on 18 July 1996, leaving 1,173 army troops dead'. The page gives the battle, not a district; the district is the researcher's reading.

29 September 1996: Kilinochchi taken. 'The town of Kilinochchi was taken on 29 September', after 'The government launched another offensive in August 1996'; the sentence does not name the force. The district outside the town stayed LTTE ground.
27 September 1998: the Tigers retake Kilinochchi. 'On 27 September 1998 the LTTE launched Operation Unceasing Waves II and, after heavy fighting, captured Kilinochchi.'

region.text: the Vanni: Mannar, Kilinochchi and Mullaitivu

ledger.note: 1999: the Vanni goes back to the Tigers. 'Nearly all the Vanni rapidly fell back into LTTE hands.' The page names the Vanni, not the districts; Mannar, Kilinochchi and Mullaitivu are the researcher's reading, and Vavuniya, named on no page, is left out. Month: the Sri Lankan civil war page places it in 'Operation Unceasing Waves III on 2 November 1999' (added by reviewer sa-06-e, 2026-10-25).

region.text: the Eastern Province: Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Ampara districts

ledger.note: 2000: the Tigers' peak. 'at its peak in 2000, the LTTE was in control of 76% of the landmass in the Northern and Eastern provinces'. Page silent on when the east came under the Tigers or which districts; the Eastern Province is bridged here from the 2007 recapture, so the reviewer should treat this as a gap. Vavuniya and Trincomalee town are named nowhere.

region.text: the Elephant Pass military complex between the Jaffna peninsula and the Vanni

ledger.note: 22 April 2000: Elephant Pass falls. 'On 22 April 2000 the Elephant Pass military complex, which had separated the Jaffna peninsula from the Vanni mainland for 17 years, fell into the hands of the LTTE'; 'After securing a vast area formerly controlled by the military, the LTTE further advanced northwards' (2001).

region.text: the Eastern Province: Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Ampara districts

ledger.note: 11 July 2007: the army takes Thoppigala and the east. 'the army captured the Thoppigala peak on 11 July 2007, ending the LTTE's military capability in the Eastern Province'; the Tigers kept 'a 140-square-kilometre pocket of jungle in the Thoppigala area'.
By 2 August 2008: Mannar District is lost by the Tigers. 'By 2 August 2008, LTTE lost the Mannar District following the fall of Vellankulam town.'

region.text: the Kilinochchi district, the Tigers' administrative capital

ledger.note: 2 January 2009: Kilinochchi captured. Troops took 'Kilinochchi, the city which the LTTE had used for over a decade as its de facto administrative capital.' The page names the city; the district is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Mullaitivu district around the town

ledger.note: 25 January 2009: Mullaitivu town captured. On 25 January 2009 troops 'completely captured' Mullaitivu town.

18 May 2009: the last pocket falls and the war ends. 'The last pocket of territory controlled by the LTTE was captured by the Sri Lankan Army on 18 May 2009'; infobox of the civil war: 'Sri Lankan government victory', 23 July 1983 - 18 May 2009. The page does not say where the pocket was; the Mullaitivu district is the researcher's reading from the January 2009 fall of Mullaitivu town.

wars.name: Sri Lankan Civil War

zones.text: the Northern and Eastern provinces: the eight districts of the claimed Tamil Eelam

wars.outcome: 'Sri Lankan government victory': the LTTE was militarily defeated in May 2009 and the government 're-established control of the entire country'. In between the Tigers held a de facto state in the north and east (the tamil-eelam rebel dossier).
wars.note: Began 23 July 1983 (infobox). Eelam War III began 19 April 1995; a Memorandum of Understanding (ceasefire) was formalised on 22 February 2002; Eelam War IV ran from 2006 to 2009. The Sri Lanka page gives no area for the LTTE's holdings; the LTTE page gives 76 percent of the Northern and Eastern provinces at the 2000 peak.

wars.name: Indian Peace Keeping Force intervention
wars.outcome: 'the Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord was signed on 29 July 1987'; the IPKF 'tried to demobilise the LTTE by force and ended up in full-scale conflict with them'; its 32-month presence ended when 'the last ship left Sri Lanka on 24 March 1990'. No land changed state.
wars.note: India held no Sri Lankan land, so no occupation event is recorded.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border.
The island's outline is sharp; the front lines between the government and the Tigers (the rebel zone of tamil-eelam) are soft and move by town and district.
An island: the coast is the border.

notes:
Written by sa-06-e on 2026-10-25 from five opened Wikipedia pages (budget 1-2): Sri Lanka and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte for the state, and the Sri Lankan civil war, Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam and Tamil Eelam pages added because the Tigers held a de facto state for about two decades and Cliopatria draws the whole island as Sri Lankan government land throughout. They also support the new rebel dossier tamil-eelam (new slug).
(1) CLIOPATRIA. One shape, 73,532 km2 for 1948-2024, matching the island; no correction. Cliopatria's British Raj row covers Ceylon until 1947 and its British Ceylon row 1796-1814 only; the british-ceylon dossier of sa-06 carries 1815-1947.
(2) REBEL LAND. The ledger's loss and gain events against tamil-eelam are district-level readings; the pages give towns and battles, not districts, and no area. Vavuniya, Trincomalee town and the Jaffna peninsula's southern strip are named by no page and are not placed. The east (2000 event) is confidence 1: the pages give the 2000 peak share and the 2007 recapture but not when the east came under the Tigers. The 2002 ceasefire (Memorandum of Understanding, 22 February 2002) is in the war entry only.
(3) NOT OPENED. The Sri Lankan Civil War page does not cover 2008-2009 (the Mannar, Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu and final-pocket events come from the LTTE and Tamil Eelam pages); the Eelam War IV page, the Vanni offensive, Operation Riviresa and the Operation Liberation of 1987 would sharpen the months.
(4) GAZETTEER. All districts resolve as Natural Earth admin-1 names (Jaffna, Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu, Mannar, Vavuniya, Batticaloa, Trincomalee, Ampara); Kachchatheevu has no place entry and a 5 km radius around it holds no land cell (sub-cell event, informational only); 'Elephant Pass' (80.4 E 9.58 N) and 'Thoppigala' have no place entry.
(5) The Katchatheevu cession is also in republic-of-india's ledger as a loss.
